name: Antigua and Barbuda
fact: Designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site, Nelson's Dockyard preserves the world's only continuously operating Georgian naval dockyard within a protected natural harbour.

name: Bahamas
fact: Covering vast expanses of clear turquoise waters, the Bahamas protects the third-longest fringing barrier reef on Earth alongside one of the planet's largest underwater cave systems.

name: Barbados
fact: Botanists first documented the grapefruit on Barbados in the eighteenth century, where it developed naturally as an accidental hybrid between the sweet orange and Indonesian pomelo.

name: Belize
fact: Belize established the world's first dedicated jaguar preserve at Cockscomb Basin, protecting hundreds of square miles of lush forest habitat for majestic wild cats.

name: Canada
fact: Canadian researchers in Toronto revolutionized modern medicine in 1921 by discovering insulin, saving millions of lives around the world from diabetes.

name: Costa Rica
fact: Pioneering global ecological stewardship, Costa Rica consistently generates more than ninety-eight percent of its electricity from renewable sources like hydro, wind, and geothermal energy.

name: Cuba
fact: Dense woodlands across Cuba shelter the bee hummingbird, the smallest living bird species on Earth, measuring barely two inches from bill to tail.

name: Dominica
fact: Dominica established the world's first marine protected area dedicated to endangered sperm whales, safeguarding essential nursing grounds along its calm western coastline.

name: Dominican Republic
fact: Every winter, thousands of North Atlantic humpback whales migrate to the warm, protected sanctuary of Samaná Bay and Silver Bank for courtship and calving.

name: El Salvador
fact: Preserved intact beneath layers of volcanic ash, the ancient village of Joya de Cerén offers archaeologists an extraordinary glimpse into daily pre-Columbian farming life.

name: Grenada
fact: Created in 2006, the Molinere Underwater Sculpture Park off Grenada became the world's first aquatic art installation, functioning as an artificial reef for marine wildlife.

name: Guatemala
fact: Ringed by three majestic volcanoes and traditional highland villages, the shimmering caldera waters of Lake Atitlán rank among Central America's most breathtaking natural wonders.

name: Haiti
fact: Lush cloud forests within Pic Macaya National Park shelter hundreds of flowering orchid varieties and rare endemic amphibians found nowhere else on the planet.

name: Honduras
fact: Situated along the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, the Bay Islands of Honduras offer world-renowned diving sites celebrated for crystalline waters and thriving sea turtle populations.

name: Jamaica
fact: Misty slopes in the Blue Mountains yield one of the globe's most prized gourmet coffees, cultivated patiently in mineral-rich volcanic soils and cool mountain breezes.

name: Mexico
fact: Every autumn, hundreds of millions of monarch butterflies complete an epic migratory journey to blanket the high-altitude oyamel fir forests of central Mexico.

name: Nicaragua
fact: Rising majestically from the freshwater expanse of Lake Nicaragua, the hourglass-shaped island of Ometepe was sculpted over millennia by two dramatic adjoining volcanoes.

name: Panama
fact: Serving as an engineering marvel of international connectivity, the Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans through an ingenious system of gravity-fed water locks.

name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
fact: The expanding rainforest of the Central Forest Reserve blankets the volcanic slopes of Saint Kitts, creating an exceptional sanctuary for vibrant Caribbean flora and birdlife.

name: Saint Lucia
fact: The iconic volcanic spires of the Pitons soar straight out of the Caribbean Sea, anchoring a celebrated UNESCO World Heritage site of remarkable natural beauty.

name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
fact: Founded in 1765, the Saint Vincent Botanical Gardens in Kingstown thrive as the oldest botanical garden in the Western Hemisphere, cultivating rare tropical trees and medicinal plants.

name: Trinidad and Tobago
fact: Trinidad and Tobago gifted acoustic music the steelpan, widely celebrated as the only major acoustic musical instrument invented during the twentieth century.

name: United States
fact: Establishing Yellowstone in 1872, the nation pioneered the concept of national parks, inspiring a worldwide conservation movement to preserve pristine wilderness for future generations.
